result.summary: Read core-directives.md and docs/agents/design/REQ-027.md in full, then git diff master...HEAD line by line against the design: domain/registration.ts's selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent (a plain SELECT with ne(admission,'withdrawn'), no join to events, no time predicate/evaluationTime param -- matches §2 exactly), handlers/event.ts's composeCancellationMessage (at-send-time freshness recheck via getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent, returns {kind:'skip'} on missing-row/withdrawn, else the 3-line join per §4) and notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants (fixed snapshot list selected once, plain sequential for...of, sendLedgeredNotification per candidate with classification:'transactional', per-call outcome not inspected -- matches §3's field/source table exactly), makeEventCancelHandler's new sender param and call-site ordering (await notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants immediately after cancelEvent returns, before ctx.reply -- matches §5), index.ts's one-line wiring reusing the existing process-wide notificationSender, and the three i18n files' single new key (cancelledNotificationHeader) with deepLinkSeeUpcoming reused unchanged (no new onward-path string, matches §4). INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC1 MYSELF with a DIFFERENT fixture shape than BACKEND-DEV's (2 admitted / 1 waitlisted / 3 withdrawn, vs. BACKEND-DEV's 3/2/1) via a scratch db test (apps/bot/src/handlers/__reviewer_verify.db.test.ts, deleted after use) against a live scratch Postgres: exactly 3 sends, exactly 3 notification_ledger rows (kind='event_cancelled'), zero ledger rows for any of the 3 withdrawn registrants (checked individually, not just aggregate count) -- confirms the filter genuinely excludes only 'withdrawn' and is not coincidentally correct for BACKEND-DEV's specific counts. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC2 MYSELF, going further than same-process repetition: after run 1 (3 sends via db/pool instance A), constructed a WHOLLY SEPARATE pg.Pool + drizzle instance (pool2/db2, no shared reference to instance A) and ran notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants against it a second time -- 0 sends, ledger unchanged at exactly 3 rows (1 per registrant). Traced the actual mechanism this rests on: sendLedgeredNotification's step 4 (domain/notification.ts lines 121-134) is a single atomic INSERT into notification_ledger, gated only by the DB's own uq_notification_ledger_registration_kind unique index (schema.ts) -- a 23505 violation is caught and returns skipped-already-sent with no send. notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants and composeCancellationMessage hold no module-level or closure-level state across calls (confirmed by reading both functions in full -- no cache, no Set, no counter). This is structurally identical to REQ-025/026's own idempotency guarantee, which WF02-REQ-026's own REVIEWER step already ran a genuine two-OS-process test against for the same underlying mechanism (sendLedgeredNotification, unchanged by this diff). Given the mechanism is unchanged and was already proven durable across a real process boundary for this exact code path, and my own fresh-Pool test here additionally confirms no per-instance-cached state was introduced by this run's new call sites, a repeated full two-`npx tsx`-process test is not warranted for every new consumer of an already-proven-durable shared primitive -- the structural argument holds. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC3 MYSELF (same scratch test file, one registrant with broadcast_opt_in explicitly false): still received exactly 1 send. Traced sendLedgeredNotification's step 3 -- the broadcastOptIn check is gated on `classification === 'marketing'` only, and notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants passes the literal 'transactional' on every call (handlers/event.ts diff, confirmed no branch varies this), so the field is structurally never read for this call path. RE-VERIFIED AC4 by direct code read rather than a new fixture (BACKEND-DEV's own AC4 test already does a full sorted-row deep-equal, which is the strongest form the property admits): confirmed by reading every function this diff adds -- selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent is SELECT-only, composeCancellationMessage's only DB call is getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent (also SELECT-only, confirmed by reading it), notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants issues no direct DB write itself (only calls sendLedgeredNotification, whose only write target is notification_ledger, not registrations). None of the three new/changed functions can write to registrations. cancelEvent (REQ-016) CONFIRMED GENUINELY UNTOUCHED: `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts` returns EMPTY (zero diff) -- not just 'unchanged in substance', the file is byte-for-byte identical to master. NOTIFICATION BATCH TRIGGERED EXACTLY ONCE PER INVOCATION: grepped every call site of cancelEvent in apps/bot/src (excluding tests) -- exactly one, inside makeEventCancelHandler itself, immediately followed by the one notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants call added by this diff. No other code path transitions events.status to 'cancelled' (cancelEvent is the only writer of that column found in domain/event.ts), so there is no route by which the batch could be re-triggered outside this one handler invocation. SYNCHRONOUS-BLOCKING DESIGN (§8 OQ4) ASSESSED: design already considered and rejected fire-and-forget (detached, un-awaited) dispatch as strictly worse (no way to surface a failed send back to the organizer, PRD 1's no-new-infrastructure stance rules out @grammyjs/runner/a job queue). I considered a narrower reordering not explicitly ruled out by §8 -- award ctx.reply BEFORE notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants instead of after -- and confirmed the call-site ordering matches the design exactly (right after cancelEvent, before ctx.reply, per §5). Reordering would let the organizer's own client see the confirmation sooner, but grammy's single-threaded long-poll loop (index.ts line ~195, no concurrent dispatcher) does not advance to the next update until the whole handler function's promise resolves regardless of which await happens first inside it -- so OTHER users' wait time is identical either order; only the organizer's own perceived latency would improve. This is a MINOR, non-blocking UX suggestion, not a correctness gap, and matches the design's own explicit specification (BACKEND-DEV followed §5's stated order exactly, this is not an implementation deviation) -- filed as a suggestion for a future design revision, not a rework demand on this run. DOMAIN-VS-HANDLER PLACEMENT (decisions/0004) CONFIRMED CORRECT: composeCancellationMessage/notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants live in handlers/event.ts, matching design §3's explicit statement that this mirrors withdraw.ts's own sendPromotionNotification placement (confirmed: grep shows sendPromotionNotification is itself defined in handlers/withdraw.ts, not domain/, an established same-shape precedent) -- not a BACKEND-DEV improvisation, the design named this placement and reasoning explicitly (composeMessage/orchestration is message-composition-and-dispatch-plumbing, not domain business-rule logic; the actual admission-eligibility rule lives in selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent, domain/registration.ts, confirmed grammy-free by reading the file's imports). WORKSPACE/BUILD-OUTPUT CHECK: `git diff master...HEAD --stat` touches only existing apps/bot/src files, docs/agents/design/, and this run's own handoffs/i18n additions -- no new npm workspace, no apps/* rename, no build-output directory moved. No scratch Docker build required per this role's trigger condition. COMMANDS RUN MYSELF, REAL OUTPUT (repo root; scratch Postgres bot-postgres-1 started and migrated by me via `npx drizzle-kit migrate` -- no new migration file generated, independently confirming the design's own 'Schema change: NO' claim): `npm run build` -> exit 0, apps/web Next.js build clean, apps/bot tsc clean. `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors (apps/web: same 2 pre-existing unrelated LCP warnings; apps/bot: 0 problems). `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, full suite) -> 24 files / 260 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- matches BACKEND-DEV's reported count exactly. My own scratch verification file (apps/bot/src/handlers/__reviewer_verify.db.test.ts) was deleted immediately after use -- `git status --porcelain` confirmed clean before writing this handoff. Scope check: diff touches exactly the design's own file list (registration.ts, event.ts, the three i18n files, index.ts, the new event.db.test.ts) plus docs/agents/design/REQ-027.md and this run's own handoffs. No scope creep. Content shape (placeholder copy, CONTENT-BA owns final wording per decisions/0002) matches convention.

issues.title: Organizer's own confirmation reply could be sent before the notification batch instead of after, with no downside to other users
issues.description: handlers/event.ts's makeEventCancelHandler awaits notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants(...) before ctx.reply(...), per design §5's explicit ordering. Since grammy's single-threaded long-poll loop (index.ts, no @grammyjs/runner concurrent dispatcher) only advances to the next update after the handler's entire promise resolves, reordering to reply-then-notify would not change how long other users wait, but would let the organizer see their own 'Event cancelled' confirmation immediately instead of after the whole batch completes. Not a correctness gap and not a deviation from the approved design -- BACKEND-DEV implemented §5 exactly as specified.
issues.recommendation: Consider this reordering the next time REQ-027's design is revisited or superseded; not worth a rework cycle on its own given zero effect on AC1-AC5 or on other users' latency.
